name: uv
tagline: A Python package and project manager written in Rust.
hook: A concise constraint list for targeted tests, fallible operations, precise lockfiles, privileged webhooks, and clear prose.
summary: uv's root file is a compact list of constraints: run targeted tests, handle fallible operations explicitly, keep dependency updates precise, protect privileged workflows, and write prose for maintainers rather than the agent conversation.

techniques.title: Keep dependency updates precise
techniques.body: The lockfile rule bans updating every dependency and names cargo update --precise as the required mechanism. It gives a concrete boundary for dependency-related diffs.
techniques.quote:
- NEVER update all dependencies in the lockfile and ALWAYS use `cargo update --precise` to make
  lockfile changes

techniques.title: Use one privileged workflow dispatcher
techniques.body: Webhook-triggered privileged work must go through the existing automation dispatcher. The adjacent rule prohibits suppressing the security lint and asks for a separate dispatcher change when an event is unsupported.
techniques.quote:
- ALWAYS use `.github/automations-dispatch.json` to trigger privileged workflows from GitHub webhook
  events instead of adding `pull_request_target` workflows
- NEVER suppress the `dangerous-triggers` security lint; extend the automation dispatcher in a
  separate pull request if it does not support the required event

techniques.title: Make new enum variants require handling
techniques.body: The guide prefers exhaustive match expressions without wildcard arms. Its stated reason is that adding an enum variant should force an explicit decision at each affected match.
techniques.quote:
- PREFER exhaustive `match` expressions without wildcard (`_`) arms over `matches!`, so new enum
  variants require explicit handling

techniques.title: Keep conversation history out of project prose
techniques.body: Comments and pull request descriptions are addressed to maintainers who did not see the conversation. The guide also favors descriptions of present behavior and rationale over references to prior iterations.
techniques.quote:
- DO NOT leak our conversation, prompt, or iteration history into code comments, pull request
  descriptions, or other maintainer-facing prose. Write for readers who have not seen our
  conversation.
- PREFER comments that explain the current behavior and rationale. Avoid past-facing wording like
  "preserve the existing behavior"; explain the actual backwards-compatibility constraint instead.

steal: Specify the narrow dependency-update operation contributors should use.
Route privileged automation through an existing reviewed entry point.
Prefer exhaustive handling where new variants need deliberate decisions.
Write project prose for readers without the agent conversation.
